value.name: lawyer postpones building decision
value.description: The lawyer says the group does not need to decide what to do with the building immediately and frames the upcoming report as only about the building's value.
evidence: "We have until next Wednesday. But the report will not say anything about you. It will say only what the building is worth."
"The conversation about what to do with the building is the conversation you three are going to have, with or without me in the room, between Wednesday and the meeting the following Monday."
value.time_hint: between Wednesday and the following Monday

value.name: lawyer urges careful discussion
value.description: The lawyer suggests they begin the conversation now while she is present because people tend to speak more carefully in front of a lawyer.
evidence: "I would like to suggest that you have at least the first part of that conversation now, while I am here,"

"I have noticed in other estates that the conversations that begin in front of a lawyer tend to be slightly more careful than the conversations that begin without one, and that the careful version, once established, tends to persist."

value.name: lawyer invites Serrano to speak
value.description: The lawyer singles out Mr. Serrano and asks him to begin the discussion.

value.name: Serrano prepares to speak
value.description: Serrano appears ready and rehearsed, but when called on he realizes his prepared response has fallen apart.
evidence: He did not look surprised to be asked.

He looked, rather, like a man who had been waiting to be asked and who had been rehearsing what he would say and who, now that the moment had come, was discovering that the rehearsal had not survived the morning.

value.name: Serrano begins reconsidering his mother's wishes
value.description: Serrano starts speaking about what he said on Monday and admits he has been rethinking his claim about what his mother would have hated.
evidence: "I have been thinking," he said, "about what I said on Monday. About my mother. About — I said she would have hated this."

value.name: Serrano admits uncertainty about mother's feelings
value.description: Serrano confesses that he no longer believes he truly knows what his mother would have hated.
evidence: "I have been thinking about that since Monday and I do not think I know what she would have hated."

value.name: Serrano distinguishes his feelings from his mother's
value.description: Serrano realizes he has been projecting his own feelings onto his mother and confusing the two for a long time.
evidence: "I think I know what I would have hated, on her behalf, and I think I have been confusing the two things for a long tim
